header: The parts every live card shares: the line that says where the numbers came from and when (I never show a number without its source and its time), a calm loading state, a plain failure with a retry, the up/down chip of a change, and a trend chart drawn as SVG with a hover read-out. Sizes are the ones of the modal's scale sheet. Nothing is stored or sent.

symbols.name: stamp
doc: Formats a time as "3:42 pm, 12 Nov", in Indian time.

members.name: live
doc: I make LIVE a solid green with a soft glow and a ping ring round its dot: it is the one thing on the card meant to catch the eye. The motion stops for people who ask their device for less.

symbols.name: StatusPill
symbols.sig: export function StatusPill({ label }: { label: FreshnessLabel })
doc: This is the one pill that says whether a figure is live, the last close, or a saved copy. The words and the colours are the same on every card; I use light fills so it reads on a dark tile and on a pale card.

doc: An up or a down arrow with the change: green or red, and grey for zero.

members.name: label
doc: The short date under the axis, e.g. "13 Jul".

members.name: full
doc: The whole date for the read-outs, e.g. "13 Jul 2026" (the label when absent).

members.name: iso
doc: YYYY-MM-DD; I use it to say how long ago the chart begins.

members.name: est
doc: Marks an estimate, not a published rate: I draw it dashed and mark it "est.".

members.name: note
doc: Said under the figure of the first day: when no figure was published for that exact day, it tells which day's figure is shown instead.

symbols.name: spanText
symbols.sig: export function spanText(fromIso?: string, toIso?: string): string
doc: Gives "4 months" / "1 year" / "3 weeks" for the span between two ISO dates; it is empty when either is missing.

symbols.name: niceTicks
symbols.sig: export function niceTicks(lo: number, hi: number, want = 4): number[]
doc: I pick round axis values: about `want` of them, on 1/2/5 steps, all inside lo..hi.

symbols.name: dateTicks
symbols.sig: export function dateTicks(n: number, want = 6): number[]
doc: Chooses which points get a date under the axis: the first, the last and evenly spaced ones between, so the dates are never crowded.

symbols.name: datesThatFit
doc: How many dates a chart of this width (in pixels) can carry under its axis without them touching. I take a date to be about 70 px wide; 0 means not measured yet.

symbols.name: edgeShift
doc: I keep a callout inside the chart: left-aligned near the left edge, right-aligned near the right edge, centred between.

symbols.name: TREND_W
doc: A line chart with an area under it that draws itself in, grid lines with round values on the left, dates along the bottom, the highest and the lowest day marked on the line with their date and value, and a read-out on hover (or touch). For a price that stays as it is until the day it is changed (fuel), `step` draws it as a staircase, because a sloping line would say the price drifted. `ties: "first"` names the DAY a high or a low was first reached, not the latest day on which it still held, and the high and the low say how long they held. The drawing's own units: I draw the points from PAD to W - PAD across a drawing W wide, so they do not touch the frame.

symbols.name: trendFraction
symbols.sig: const trendFraction = (i: number, n: number): number =>
doc: Where on the drawing (0 at its left edge, 1 at its right) the i-th of n points is drawn.

symbols.name: trendIndex
symbols.sig: export function trendIndex(fraction: number, n: number): number
doc: Finds the point nearest to a place on the drawing (0 to 1 from its left edge). It is the inverse of trendFraction, so the dot is drawn at the place the pointer is; a pointer over the padding takes the first or the last point.
